The '''Y-45 armored transport hauler''', also known as the '''AT-hauler''' or the '''AT tug''', was a specialized [[starship]] manufactured by [[Kuat Drive Yards]] for use in the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Army|army]]. Boasting cargo lifter arms, it was used for swift [[Dropship|deployment]] of [[walker]]s onto the battlefield. After the [[Battle of Yavin]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] managed to salvage several Y-45s.

==Characteristics==
The Y-45 armored transport hauler, also known as AT-hauler, was built by [[Kuat Drive Yards]],<ref name="TOG" /> one of the foremost military shipwrights in [[the galaxy]],<ref name="Ultimate">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> for use by the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TOG" />

[[File:AThaulerparked-SASWSOCE.png|thumb|left|200px|An AT-hauler with gantry arms lifted for docking]]
Several [[ion engine]]s provided the ship with thrust in [[realspace]], while linked banks of [[repulsorlift]] generators gave it thrust and lift in [[atmosphere]]. Its maximum atmospheric speed was 125 [[Kilometer per hour|kilometers per hour]]. The ship also had a [[hyperdrive]], although its [[navigation computer]] only contained pre-calculated [[hyperspace]] jump destinations to a select group of Imperial outposts—in an effort to discourage [[Thief|thieves]].<ref name="TOG" />

Its heavy-duty cargo lifter arms featured magnetic clamps on the underside that locked around the cargo. The load could be further secured by localized traction fields, as well as strong cable ties and winches of [[Steelton]] make. Energized tensile strength fields radiating through the arms helped the Y-45 withstand buckling under heavy weights.<ref name="TOG" />

Not unlike [[Sienar Fleet Systems]]'s [[Abecederian line]] of [[shuttle]]s, the Y-45 could rotate its arms upward in landing mode, to save space in [[hangar]] bays and landing fields. As such, it measured 20.10 [[meter]]s in length and 6.50 in height in flight mode (with both arms extended), but 11.20 meters in length and 18.90 in height in landing mode (with both arms upward).<ref name="TOG" />

Other notable features of the Y-45 included its [[armor]]ed [[cockpit]] canopy with forward and downward [[viewport]]s, a service gantry and clamp brace platform, and a [[shower]] stall inside the main compartment.<ref name="TOG" />

The Y-45 required a crew of only two: a [[pilot]] to handle the flight operations, and a co-pilot to manage the cargo-lifting operations.<ref name="TOG" />

==Role==
[[File:AThauler-Fathead.png|thumb|right|250px|An AT-hauler view showing the heavy-duty magnetic clamps]]
The Y-45 was designed for swift [[Dropship|deployment]] of [[walker]]s<ref name="DB" /> anywhere onto the battlefield, except under an [[Deflector shield|energy shield]].<ref name="Commander" /> It could either carry one [[All Terrain Defense Turret]],<ref name="Solo" /> one [[All Terrain Scout Transport]],<ref name="JFO" /> two [[2-M Saber-class repulsor tank|2-M Hover Tanks]], or even one [[All Terrain Armored Transport]].<ref name="Commander" />

==History==
In [[14 BBY]],<ref name="JFO Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' to [[14 BBY]].</ref> a Y-45 delivered an [[All Terrain Scout Transport]] on [[Kashyyyk]] to deal with an attack on the Imperial Refinery lead by [[Saw Gerrera]] and his [[Partisans]].<ref name="JFO" />

The Y-45 armored transport haulers were introduced to replace [[Clone Wars]]-era carriers,<ref name="TOG" /> but by [[10 BBY]]<ref name="Solo Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' to [[10 BBY]].</ref> they were already in the process of being phased out themselves in favor of more versatile transports.<ref name="TOG" /> Nevertheless, they still saw action on [[Mimban]]<ref name="Solo" /> in that [[Standard year|year]],<ref name="Solo Date" /> during an Imperial [[Mimban Campaign|campaign]] against the native [[Mimbanese]] where one was seen deploying an AT-DT.<ref name="Solo" />

[[File:HeistonVandor-SASWS.png|thumb|left|240px|Beckett's gang used a stolen Y-45 on a job on Vandor.]]
The [[gangster]] [[Tobias Beckett]] and his [[Beckett's gang|crew]] stole a Y-45 from the [[224th Imperial Armored Division|Imperial forces]] on Mimban to [[Heist on Vandor|grab]] a shipment of [[coaxium]] from a passing [[20-T Railcrawler conveyex transport|conveyex]] [[train]] on [[Vandor]]. However, the heist quickly complicated when the [[Cloud-Riders]] also attacked the train, wanting the coaxium for their own uses. The Y-45 was boarded by Imperials, where the crew member Durant was shot and killed, dying next to the crew's recent addition, [[Han Solo]]. At the same time, an explosion caused by [[Val]] on the tracks resulted in the train plummeting. Solo attempted to lift off with the Y-45, along with Beckett and the coaxium, but failed as the shipment was slammed into a mountain, causing a large explosion. The AT-hauler was destroyed in a crash, as Solo and Beckett survived.<ref name="Solo" />

Some time after the [[Battle of Yavin]], the anti-Empire [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] salvaged several Y-45s, which they put to work on the battlefield. The Alliance notably used them to deploy [[Armored Assault Tank Mk I|Armored Assault Tanks]] and [[Juggernaut (Rebel Alliance)|juggernauts]]. Rather than the standard Imperial light [[Color|gray]], those Alliance haulers were colored dark gray and orange.<ref name="Commander" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Salvaged_AT-hauler_-_Star_Wars_Commander.png|thumb|right|185px|A salvaged AT-hauler used by the Alliance to Restore the Republic.]]{{Quote|It's essentially a flying crane, really. It's utilitarian. It's not the coolest thing you're going to find [aesthetically], but what I think is cool about it is it's kind of like a Swiss army knife. It has a couple different functions to it.|James Clyne|<ref name="Designing Solo pt3">{{SW|url=news/designing-solo-a-star-wars-story-part-3-conveyex-train-heist|text=Designing ''Solo: A Star Wars Story'', Part 3: Pulling Off the Train Heist}}</ref>}}
The Y-45 armored transport hauler was created for ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', a [[Star Wars Anthology Series|stand-alone]] ''[[Star Wars]]'' film directed by [[Ron Howard]] that was released worldwide on [[May 25]], [[2018]]. Its design went through several iterations, the last of which was infused with a 1970s design sensibility. [[James Clyne]], [[Lucasfilm]]'s design supervisor for ''Solo'', described it as a utilitarian, "[[Wikipedia:Swiss Army knife|Swiss army knife]]" of a ship. It was he who added the caged gantry to the bottom, and came up with the arms' stiff movements, which were inspired by an image of [[Wikipedia:Frankenstein's monster|Frankenstein's monster]].<ref name="Designing Solo pt3" /> Two of the early inspirations for the transport hauler, were the [[W:c:tron:Recognizer|Recognizer]] from the [[1982]] cult film [[W:c:tron:TRON|''TRON'']] and the [[Wikipedia:United States Army|United States Army's]] [[Wikipedia:Sikorsky CH-54 Tarhe|Sikorsky CH-54 Tarhe]] helicopter.<ref name="Art of Solo">''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>
